headline: Markets Brace for Inflation Data as Geopolitical Fog Thickens Around Shipping Lanes
body_html:
Futures point to a cautious open on this Friday morning as traders absorb a bruising Thursday session that saw sellers dominate across the board — 416 names lower against just 128 advancers in our 545-stock universe. Every sector closed in the red, with Homebuilders off 2.34% leading the damage and Software the relative shelter at minus 0.37%. The day's standout bright spots were clustered in radio-frequency and audio chip names, with Skyworks Solutions surging 9.79% and Qorvo adding 6.77%, suggesting company-specific catalysts rather than any broad risk appetite.

The session's decisive macro overhang carries directly into Friday's open: Treasury yields held steady Thursday as markets positioned ahead of this morning's consumer inflation print. That report lands as the most consequential near-term catalyst, capable of reshaping rate expectations heading into month-end. Oil markets add a second layer of complexity — crude is on track for a weekly gain exceeding 7%, with U.S. diesel at a record high, as supply disruptions tied to Middle East conflict ripple through energy markets.

Geopolitics will continue commanding attention at the open. Houthi forces have reached a position on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, one of global shipping's most critical chokepoints, and Hormuz traffic has fallen to single-digit vessel counts. Watch energy names and any freight-exposed industrials for early directional signals when trading begins.

briefs.headline: CPI Report Is the Morning's Defining Moment
briefs.body: This morning's consumer price index release is the single data point markets have been circling all week. Treasury yields held their ground through Thursday's session as traders chose to wait rather than commit. A hotter-than-expected reading could rattle rate-sensitive sectors that are already under pressure from Thursday's broad selloff.

briefs.headline: Houthi Advance on Bab el-Mandeb Puts Shipping Costs Back in Focus
briefs.body: Houthi forces have moved onto Yemen's Dhubab, placing them at the mouth of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait — a narrow corridor through which a substantial share of global seaborne trade passes. The development compounds existing stress on Hormuz, where vessel traffic has fallen to single-digit counts, and underpins crude oil's trajectory toward a weekly gain of more than 7%.

briefs.headline: Oil's Weekly Surge Pushes Diesel to Uncharted Territory
briefs.body: Crude is poised to close out the week with gains exceeding 7% as conflict-driven supply disruptions tighten the market. U.S. diesel prices have hit a record high in the process, a development with direct pass-through implications for transportation, agriculture, and manufacturing costs across the broader economy.

briefs.headline: RF Chip Names Buck the Selloff With Sharp Single-Day Moves
briefs.body: Skyworks Solutions and Qorvo posted gains of 9.79% and 6.77% respectively on Thursday, standing out sharply against an otherwise deeply negative tape. Cirrus Logic added another 5.20%, reinforcing the move in semiconductor-adjacent hardware. The cluster of strength in these names points to company-specific news flow rather than any sector-wide tailwind.

briefs.headline: Apparel Retailers Take the Heaviest Blows on Thursday
briefs.body: American Eagle Outfitters tumbled 13.97% — the steepest single-session decline in our universe Thursday — while Abercrombie & Fitch shed 6.02%. The paired declines dragged the broader Consumer sector down 1.46% for the day, raising questions about the demand backdrop heading into the autumn retail season.

briefs.headline: UAE Rethinks AI Infrastructure After Iranian Strikes
briefs.body: The United Arab Emirates is revising its artificial intelligence data center buildout following Iranian attacks, according to reporting published ahead of Friday's open. The development signals that the regional conflict is beginning to reshape capital allocation decisions in the fast-growing Gulf technology sector, with potential downstream effects on global AI infrastructure timelines.
